title: How to Check How Many Mobile SIMs Are Registered to Your Name via TAFCOP

faq.title: What is the legal limit on how many SIM cards one person can own in India?
faq.description: Under Department of Telecommunications (DoT) regulations, an individual citizen can register a maximum of 9 mobile connections across all telecom operators combined (Jio, Airtel, Vi, BSNL). For Jammu & Kashmir, Assam, and the North East telecom circles, the statutory ceiling is restricted to 6 mobile SIM connections.

faq.title: What should I do if TAFCOP shows a phone number I don't recognize?
faq.description: Select the checkbox next to the unfamiliar number, choose the radio option 'Not My Number', and click 'Report'. The DoT generates a Ticket Reference ID and immediately instructs the respective carrier to initiate immediate re-verification; if the holder cannot produce valid physical Aadhaar biometrics within the notice period, the connection is permanently deactivated.

faq.title: Does TAFCOP display SIM cards registered to my PAN card or Passport?
faq.description: Yes. TAFCOP links all subscriber identity records submitted during Customer Acquisition Forms (CAF), whether e-KYC was executed via Aadhaar OTP, biometric fingerprint scan, or physical passport/voter ID documentation across all telecom circles.

html:
The Hidden Threat of Ghost SIM Cards

In India's rapidly evolving cybercrime ecosystem, the most prized commodity for criminal syndicates is not compromised passwords or credit card numbers; it is Aadhaar-linked mobile SIM cards. Every sophisticated cyber fraud—including WhatsApp investment traps, fake courier customs calls, digital arrest extortion schemes, and unauthorized banking OTP intercepts—requires an active cellular phone number registered to a real identity to bypass carrier fraud filters.

To acquire these connections, criminal networks collaborate with rogue SIM retail kiosks or harvest photocopies of Aadhaar cards submitted for hotel registrations, property leases, or loan applications. By manipulating Point of Sale (PoS) biometric verification or forging identity forms, syndicates activate secondary 'ghost' SIM cards in your name without your knowledge. If a ghost SIM is subsequently used in a cybercrime syndicate or financial extortion racket, local police cyber cells trace the Subscriber Acquisition Form directly to your doorstep. This definitive guide demonstrates how to audit every mobile number registered to your identity using the Department of Telecommunications' official TAFCOP portal and permanently terminate fraudulent connections.

What Is TAFCOP and How Does the Database Operate?

The Telecom Analytics for Fraud management and Consumer Protection (TAFCOP) portal is a sovereign consumer defense utility built and maintained by the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) under the broader Sanchar Saathi initiative.

Historically, each telecom operator (Reliance Jio, Bharti Airtel, Vodafone Idea, and BSNL/MTNL) maintained segregated subscriber databases. A citizen had no unified mechanism to discover if a rogue agent at an Airtel kiosk had activated a supplementary Jio number using their credentials. TAFCOP continuously ingests and aggregates the Customer Acquisition Form (CAF) ledgers across all 22 Indian telecom circles. By cross-referencing your primary mobile number against centralized subscriber registries, TAFCOP instantly surfaces every single mobile number actively linked to your identity documents.

Statutory Limits: The 9-SIM Regulatory Rule

Under Government of India telecom mandates, strict thresholds govern individual mobile ownership:

  • Standard Circles: A maximum of 9 active mobile connections per individual identity across all telecom service providers combined.
  • Sensitive Border Circles: In Jammu & Kashmir, Assam, and North East telecom circles, the legal ceiling is restricted to 6 active connections.
  • Penalties for Excess SIMs: If an identity exceeds these limits without enterprise corporate authorization, carriers are mandated to disconnect all excess connections, and individuals face potential blacklisting from future telecommunications services.

Step-by-Step: Auditing Your Registered Numbers on TAFCOP

The auditing procedure requires zero paperwork and takes under 120 seconds to complete from any smartphone or computer browser:

  1. Open your browser and navigate directly to the official government portal: https://tafcop.sancharsaathi.gov.in (or access via sanchar-saathi.gov.in and click TAFCOP).
  2. Enter Your Primary Mobile Number: In the input box labeled 'Enter your Mobile Number', type the primary 10-digit smartphone number that you have actively used and physically possessed for several years (ideally the number linked to your bank and Aadhaar profile).
  3. Complete the Captcha Challenge: Enter the dynamic alphanumeric captcha code displayed on screen and click Validate Captcha.
  4. Verify Government OTP: You will receive a 6-digit one-time password from the sender ID DOTGOV. Enter the OTP into the verification box and click Login.
  5. Review the Active Numbers Ledger: Upon successful authentication, TAFCOP will display a structured card listing every mobile number currently active under your identity. For privacy and security, the portal masks the middle four digits (e.g., 98XXXX4215, 94XXXX8812), while displaying the first two and final four digits alongside the respective telecom operator.

How to Report and Disconnect Unauthorized Numbers

Carefully scrutinize the list with your family members. If you discover a phone number that neither you nor your dependents ever purchased:

  1. Locate the unfamiliar mobile number on the dashboard.
  2. Select the small checkbox on the extreme left of that specific phone row.
  3. Select the appropriate classification radio button:
    • Not My Number: Choose this option if you have zero knowledge of this connection and never authorized its purchase. This flags the number as an immediate identity theft / ghost connection.
    • Not Required: Choose this option if the number was legitimately purchased by you in the past (e.g., an old dongle SIM, a retired backup phone number, or a college connection) that you no longer use and wish to surrender.
    • Required: Choose this to confirm that the number is active, legitimate, and in your daily possession.
  4. Click the blue Report button at the bottom of the page.
  5. A confirmation modal will appear. Tap OK.
  6. The portal will immediately generate a unique Ticket Reference Number (e.g., TC-2026-894120). Take a screenshot or record this reference code.

TAFCOP Reporting Status Matrix

Report Classification Carrier Action Protocol Timeline to Resolution Subscriber Impact
Not My Number Telecom carrier sends mandatory biometric re-verification SMS notice to the number Immediate flagging; 30-day disconnection if re-verification fails Protects you from legal liability if the ghost SIM is used in cybercrime
Not Required Graceful telecom service termination and number release Processed at the conclusion of the active billing / validity cycle Frees up your statutory 9-SIM quota for future legitimate purchases
Required Connection verified as compliant in DoT master ledger Instantaneous confirmation Maintains uninterrupted cellular voice, SMS, and 5G data services

What Transpires After You File a TAFCOP Report?

Once your report is logged in the Department of Telecommunications central registry, an automated compliance ticket is transmitted to the nodal officer of the specific telecom carrier (Jio, Airtel, Vi, or BSNL):

  1. The carrier issues an automated SMS notice to the reported telephone number instructing the holder to visit an authorized company retail store within 30 days with original physical identity proof and biometric fingerprint authentication.
  2. Because fraudulent ghost SIM users cannot produce the legitimate Aadhaar holder's physical thumbprint or facial biometric, the number cannot be re-verified.
  3. Outgoing voice and data services are suspended within 14 days, and the connection is permanently deactivated from telecom switches at the end of the 30-day statutory notice period.
  4. You can track the live progress of your complaint at any time by revisiting the TAFCOP homepage, entering your primary mobile number, and inputting your Ticket Reference Number in the 'Track Report' box.

The Underground Mule SIM Economy in Jamtara, Mewat, and Cyber Hubs

To appreciate why TAFCOP is essential, you must understand the shadow financial economy operating behind ghost phone numbers. In notorious cybercrime hubs across India—including the Mewat region (covering parts of Haryana and Rajasthan), Jamtara (Jharkhand), and organized call centers in West Bengal—physical SIM cards are traded like liquid currency. On underground Telegram channels and localized black markets, an active mobile SIM card verified against a clean, unsuspecting citizen's Aadhaar fetches between ₹2,000 and ₹6,000 per card.

Cybercrime syndicates burn through SIM cards at an astonishing velocity. Because telecom anti-fraud filters flag numbers that place hundreds of outbound automated calls or receive immediate UPI payment disputes, a single burner SIM has an operational lifespan of only 3 to 14 days before being dropped. By fraudulently activating 50 or 100 SIM cards against harvested identity databases, a corrupt telecom retailer can generate lakhs of rupees in illicit commissions while leaving innocent citizens legally vulnerable to cybercrime summons.

Escalation Protocol: What to Do If Carriers Fail to Disconnect

While the TAFCOP portal provides a direct pipeline to telecom compliance desks, occasional administrative delays occur where an operator fails to process the deactivation within the statutory 30-day notice window. If an unauthorized number continues to appear on your TAFCOP dashboard upon subsequent audits, execute this formal escalation path:

  1. File an Appellate Grievance with the Telecom Carrier: Every licensed telecom provider maintains an internal Appellate Authority. Visit the official website of the operator (e.g., Jio Appellate Authority or Airtel Appellate Management), provide your original TAFCOP Ticket Reference ID, and lodge a formal demand for immediate carrier-level line termination.
  2. Lodge a National Grievance on CPGRAMS: The Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS) (hosted at pgportal.gov.in) is the highest administrative grievance portal of the Government of India. Select the Department of Telecommunications, cite your TAFCOP Ticket Reference ID, and state that an unauthorized cellular line remains active despite non-verification. CPGRAMS complaints mandate formal written responses from senior carrier directors within 21 business days.
  3. Obtain a Non-Involvement Certificate: If police cyber cells contact you regarding a crime committed with a ghost number, present your original TAFCOP submission confirmation and CPGRAMS complaint number. Under Indian evidentiary jurisprudence, an official timestamped government portal report filed prior to the cybercrime constitutes definitive proof of identity misappropriation and absence of criminal mens rea.

Essential Post-Audit Hardening Steps

If you discovered fraudulent connections registered against your identity, you must immediately take preventative measures to ensure your primary documents cannot be exploited again:

  • Lock Your Aadhaar Biometrics Immediately: Prevent anyone from using your fingerprint or iris data to execute fraudulent e-KYC activations by following our comprehensive guide on locking your Aadhaar biometrics via mAadhaar.
  • Report Stolen Devices to CEIR: If an unauthorized SIM was activated using details from a phone that was stolen or lost, blacklist the physical handset across all Indian telecom circles following our tutorial on finding your IMEI and blocking a stolen phone via the CEIR portal.
  • File an Information Report with Police: If multiple unauthorized SIM cards were discovered, submit an online cybercrime complaint at cybercrime.gov.in or call the 1930 helpline following our step-by-step 1930 reporting protocol. Having a formal police acknowledgement receipt provides absolute legal indemnity against downstream criminal actions committed using those numbers.
  • Audit Your Telecom DND Status: Stop telemarketing spam and fraudulent cold calls on your legitimate lines by reading our tutorial on activating full DND across Jio, Airtel, and Vi via 1909.
